# Formatting Rules

These rules apply to ALL document types generated by the `document` skill.

## Header Hierarchy

| Level | Usage | TOC? |
|-------|-------|------|
| `#` H1 | Document title. Exactly one per document. | Yes |
| `##` H2 | Major sections only. Keep to 5–8 per document. | Yes |
| `###` H3 | Subsections — use sparingly. Ask: can a **bold line** + bullets replace this? If yes, skip the header. | No |
| `####` H4 | **FORBIDDEN.** Never use. Replace with **bold text** on its own line followed by content. | — |
| `#####` H5+ | **FORBIDDEN.** | — |

## Table of Contents

- Include ONLY when the user explicitly requests it.
- Build the TOC from H1 and H2 headers only.
- Use Markdown anchor links: `- [Section Name](#section-name)`.
- Place the TOC immediately after the title (H1) and any introductory sentence.

## Replacing H4 with Alternatives

Instead of:
```markdown
#### Database Configuration
Some details here.
```

Use **bold text + content**:
```markdown
**Database Configuration**

Some details here, structured as a bullet list or table when possible.
```

Or use a **table** when comparing options:
```markdown
| Setting | Value | Notes |
|---------|-------|-------|
| Host | `localhost` | Override via `DB_HOST` env var |
| Port | `5432` | Default PostgreSQL port |
```

## Callout Blocks

Use blockquote-based callouts for emphasis. These render well in GitHub, Confluence (via paste), and Dropbox Paper.

```markdown
> **Note:** Informational content that adds context.

> **Warning:** Something the reader must be aware of to avoid problems.

> **Tip:** A helpful suggestion or shortcut.

> **Important:** Critical information that affects behaviour or correctness.
```

## Diagram Placeholders

When the user opted in to diagram placeholders, insert blocks like this — never auto-generate the diagram itself:

```markdown
> **📊 Diagram placeholder:** {{describe what diagram goes here, or paste a Mermaid block later}}
```

Place one placeholder per logical diagram needed (e.g. system architecture, sequence flow, data model). Do not insert more than 3 placeholders without strong justification.

## Links

- Use inline links: `[visible text](url)` — not reference-style `[text][ref]`.
- Link on FIRST mention of a concept, not every mention.
- Prefer relative links for workspace docs: `[example](../sibling-doc.md)`.
- Use full URLs for external resources.
- Add "See also" references inline after the relevant paragraph, not collected at the bottom.

## Code Blocks

- Always specify the language: ` ```typescript `, ` ```json `, ` ```bash `.
- Keep code blocks short (under 30 lines). Use `<details>` for longer snippets.
- Add a brief description before each code block explaining what it shows.

## Tables

- Use tables instead of nested headers whenever you are listing structured data.
- Keep tables under 6 columns for readability.
- Align columns with pipes and dashes (standard Markdown table syntax).

## Collapsible Sections

Use `<details>` for supplementary content that would otherwise make the doc too long:

```markdown
<details>
<summary>Click to expand: Full configuration example</summary>

Content goes here.

</details>
```

## Length Guidelines

| Document type | Target length |
|---|---|
| JIRA ticket | 100–300 words |
| README | 300–800 words |
| Confluence page | 500–2000 words |
| Dropbox Paper / Other | 300–1500 words |

These are guidelines, not hard limits. Prioritise clarity over brevity.
